title: Twist an Oreo open, one hand holding the top wafer while the other turns the base, and lay both halves on the plate
instruction: Open this Oreo into its two halves and put both halves on the plate.
context: Twisting an Oreo open is a near-universal habit (the brand's own 'twist, lick, dunk'). Physically it is torsional failure of the creme: the wafers must be counter-rotated about their shared axis (about 0.1 N m) and the creme lets go of one wafer (Owens et al., Phys. Fluids 2022). Pulling or prying a 3.5 mm wafer held only at its rim does not open it; one hand must hold one wafer still while the other turns the other.
setup: Units cm, kg; x forward from the arm bases, y left; table top 74.75 cm up. Task objects: Nabisco Oreo Original sandwich cookie lying flat on the table at (44, 0): two chocolate wafers 4.4 dia x 0.35 (top 0.0039; base 0.0039 with the creme), white creme disc 3.5 dia x 0.4 on the base wafer, 1.1 thick overall, 0.0113 in all. Plastic plate (SimReady), 17.2 x 17.7 x 2.6, 0.15, centred at (25, 0). Distractors, ignored by scoring (SimReady): 8 oz drinking glass 6.6 dia x 10, 0.40, at (52, 17); plastic spoon 15.7 x 3.5 x 1.1, 0.02, at (53, -15) yaw 1.2 rad; ceramic mug 11.4 x 9 x 8, 0.30, at (12, 25).
scoring: Opened = the two wafers were turned at least 10 degrees against each other and have separated. 0 if the cookie was never opened, or a half ever fell off the table (centre over 3 cm below the table top). 1.0: opened; both halves on the plate (each centre within 64 mm of the plate's centre and at most 12 mm above its underside), each lying flat (within 20 degrees, either face up), centres at least 45 mm apart, every fingertip at least 3 cm from both halves, both halves still, all held 1 s. 0.75: opened and both halves on the plate with the fingertips 3 cm clear, without the rest of 1.0. 0.5: opened, otherwise (a half still held, or off the plate).
reset_notes: Each trial consumes one cookie: use a fresh Oreo from the same pack, laid flat on its tape mark with the base wafer (the one the creme stays on in a test twist from that pack) down. Wipe the plate of crumbs.
fidelity: The wafers are rigid 16-sided discs at the cookie's size and mass (SimReady has no Oreo). The creme is one twist joint: a torsion spring that lets go for good past 10 degrees at 0.1 N m (Owens et al. 2022); it is rigid in pull and bending, so the creme always stays on the base wafer and wafers cannot crack or crumble. Grip force is not limited or scored. Plate and distractors are SimReady props.
